stemMd:
**Text 1**
An archive should digitize its most requested documents first. Doing so would immediately reduce handling of fragile originals while serving the largest number of current users.

**Text 2**
Request counts reflect what users already know exists. If digitization follows those counts alone, poorly catalogued collections may remain invisible. Some priority should therefore go to materials whose potential users have not yet been able to discover them.

How would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to Text 1?

options.label: A
options.textMd: By denying that digitization can reduce handling.

options.label: B
options.textMd: By arguing that present demand is useful but incomplete as a guide because discoverability affects requests.

options.label: C
options.textMd: By claiming that frequently requested documents have no value.

options.label: D
options.textMd: By insisting that no document should ever be digitized.

explanationMd: Text 2 identifies a feedback loop: known materials generate requests, which generate further visibility. That qualifies the proposed priority without rejecting digitization or the value of reducing handling.

distractorRationale.a: Text 2 does not challenge that benefit.
distractorRationale.c: It argues against using demand alone, not against serving existing users.
distractorRationale.d: It advocates a broader digitization priority.
